approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds fresh molecular graphs from the best scored molecules in the current session, using connected-fragment crossover and short sampled mutation walks. Canonical identity checks, duplicate rejection and its inherited sulfur rule admit a pool of 160 candidates. A Gaussian process regresses all accepted scores on integer-count Morgan fingerprints with generalized Tanimoto covariance. Each batch position takes the highest available value from a correlated posterior draw. After three batches without an incumbent improvement, only the forty highest predictive means remain eligible until progress resumes. Actual scores update the archive and sixty-four surviving breeders. A dormant rejection-dependent mutation floor has already been removed.
approach.novelty: Replace score regression with one local preference posterior: each accepted molecule is compared with its most similar earlier accepted molecule, and a probit Gaussian process learns their ordering with joint Laplace uncertainty. The inherited sampled allocator then consumes that new distribution. This changes the likelihood and the resulting uncertainty, unlike a transformation of regression targets. Same-Parent siblings changed allocation objectives, removed selected mean or residual consumers, shortened mutation walks, or replaced the controller with regional or tree search. The earlier neural ranker also introduced UCB allocation and ordered paid labels worse. This test uses a fixed count-kernel prior and retains correlated Thompson allocation. Its hypothesis is that local ordering improves actual purchased-batch ranking and useful progress; the existing evidence has not established that raw-score regression is defective.

observed_bottleneck: The limiting behavior is incomplete conversion of accepted-label guidance into further useful incumbent improvements, despite a functioning predictor and allocator. The actual code Parent n-cf8d309c06de has complete mean 0.607030316211131 and population SD 0.030175277546149237; its three summary.json and run.log files report successful complete sessions, no invalid or duplicate purchases, and seed macros 0.649701282562401, 0.585233817344553 and 0.586155848726439. A read-only audit of every Parent task log and trusted trajectory, recorded in policy/scratch/r0061-01-improve-L01/parent-ordering-audit.json with fifteen audit-seed-N-task.json files and their exact underlying input paths, finds 435 successful fits, zero fallbacks, zero paid prediction join errors and 4350 purchased offspring. Preannouncement mean ordering is correct for 13773 of 19495 non-tied within-purchase-batch pairs (0.7064888432931521; 80 raw-score ties excluded; no predicted ties); full cell accuracies range from 0.5993860322333078 to 0.8449731389102072. Full incumbent-increment mass is 5.978073077532332 across 253 positive events, but late ordinals146..290 contribute 1.0224077547621127 across 76 events over 2175 purchases. This is an informative but imperfect selected-stream ordering reference, not evidence of a causal regression misfit. On the same Parent, n-2d61abf0b2bd and n-7d9afd9af925 remove restricted and unrestricted residual influence and lose 0.018621410181405656 and 0.09438631107688404 in complete mean, supporting retention of sampled alternatives under their respective conditions. n-698a02f85be1 executes expected-improvement pricing but loses full gain and concentrates its useful gains near already accepted molecules; locality motivates the frozen comparison adaptation but is not an identified mediator. The earlier n-ccb8d255bf00 neural-ranker/UCB recipe activates yet has pair accuracy 0.470128 versus its same-state passive GP 0.706399 and weaker useful gains, with two endpoints missing. That is a specific counterexample to its joint recipe, not to every preference model. These observations support the ticket-selected, distinct kernel-likelihood test without borrowing failed neural capability or claiming a chemical ceiling.

adoptions.applicability: Only accepted within-session scores form preference labels. The paper supports the inference construction, not this sparse edge rule, the count kernel, deterministic score-derived preference assumptions or molecular endpoint gains.

deviations.paper_setting: General observed preferences and a GP kernel with evidence-based hyperparameter adaptation.
deviations.reason: The ticket isolates a task-local observation-model component within the existing budget and forbids hyperparameter search; local sparse edges are the explicit adaptation under test.

adoptions.applicability: The official release confirms implementability of the model class. Our canonical-record preservation, fixed count kernel and numerical procedure differ from library defaults and must be checked independently.
adoptions.borrowed_element: An official probit PairwiseGP interface with Laplace posterior and configurable covariance is a concrete implementation reference.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse the ticket-frozen search-policy review and its recorded queries rather than claim a new search. Both cited primary/official URLs were opened during planning. Adopt the probit/MAP/Laplace construction and its official model-interface precedent. Internal Parent receipts and specific earlier counterexamples motivate the sparse local adaptation and preserved sampled allocator. method_change.previous_method: The actual code Parent n-cf8d309c06de fits Gaussian regression to normalized accepted raw scores using the fixed count-Morgan generalized-Tanimoto covariance and observation-noise SD0.05.
method_change.proposed_method: Replace that active posterior component with sparse chronological nearest-predecessor probit GP utility fitting and full Laplace predictive covariance; retain raw-score graph feedback and correlated Thompson allocation.
method_change.rationale: The actual code Parent is cited in used_evidence_node_ids. Its useful but imperfect paid ordering and limited late full-path gains, current same-host residual-removal losses, useful-neighborhood observations, and the specific neural/UCB ordering failure make the frozen local kernel-likelihood model a distinguishable experiment. The test changes one posterior component; the passive original GP is measurement only. No raw-regression defect or transferable superiority of preference learning is assumed.

hypothesis: One posterior-component replacement on n-cf8d309c06de: use a zero-mean, unit-amplitude count-Tanimoto GP latent utility with likelihood product_e Phi(f_w(e)-f_l(e)) over sparse chronological local comparisons. At each inherited refit, retain all canonical accepted records in serial order; for each i>0 choose j<i maximizing the original count-kernel similarity, with earliest accepted serial breaking exact similarity ties. Choose j without scores, orient the one edge by exact raw-score order, and omit it if the two raw scores are exactly tied, without searching for another predecessor. Each pair has a unique later endpoint, at most N-1 edges are stored, and no transitive or repeated likelihood factors are manufactured. The individual preference-noise SD is 1/sqrt(2), so the pairwise probit argument has denominator1. Score magnitudes do not enter this active likelihood. With K+jI=LL^T from the inherited prior jitter ladder, f=L u and A=D L (D has +1 at the winner and -1 at the loser), minimize J(u)=0.5*u^T*u-sum(log Phi(Au)). From deterministic u=0, bounded damped Newton uses the exact gradient and Hessian; only a converged MAP may supply a fitted posterior. Let z=A u, r=phi(z)/Phi(z), W=diag(r*(r+z)), and H=I+A^T W A at MAP. The latent posterior covariance is L H^-1 L^T. For a fresh pool let V=L^-1 K_train,pool; the full predictive mean is V^T u and covariance is K_pool,pool-V^T V+V^T H^-1 V. This retains all cross-candidate terms; neither a diagonal approximation nor the regression noise0.05 enters the active likelihood. Zero non-tied edges produce the explicitly reported zero-mean GP prior. Distinct canonical records with identical count features remain distinct training records and labels. The resulting latent utility distribution, with an optional shared positive raw-location/scale interface wrapper fixed below, feeds the unchanged correlated sampled-row maxima, exact pool-order ties and K=3/M=40 eligibility law. Real raw scores alone continue to govern breeding, survival and stall state. Local ordering can therefore change paid identities and subsequent learning without changing generator support or introducing another acquisition objective; the asserted benefit remains empirical.

finding_summary.headline: Preference fits changed every batch, but worsened paid ordering and full progress
finding_summary.insights: This settles the specified sparse local probit/Laplace intervention: it runs correctly and changes consequential choices, yet supplies weaker ordering on its own purchased labels and less total useful progress. The borrowed GP-preference and Laplace elements operated; the local edge rule, fixed count prior, unit comparison scale and retained sampled allocator are adaptations, so the result does not generalize to all preference learning or the cited library’s defaults. More parent-beating offspring (762 versus 634) were produced against weaker realized generating parents, which explains why that diagnostic cannot rescue the endpoint loss. The method’s measured limitation is an inferior ranking model on both restricted and unrestricted purchased streams. A different observation/comparison model would be needed to address that limitation; this experiment does not isolate whether sparse edges, discarded score magnitudes or their covariance are responsible. Chemistry shows broader scaffold coverage (1994 typed scaffolds versus 1667) and lower fragment-excluded similarity, alongside 176 molecules above fifty heavy atoms versus 44 and unresolved stereochemistry/reactive connectivity. Thus lack of structural variety is not the demonstrated bottleneck; coherent growth and functional-group-aware proposal operators are a separate capability suggested by the observed oversized assemblies, not a proven cure. The passive comparator supplies no unpurchased rewards or alternative adaptive path, and full gain telescopes to the endpoints. The isolated contribution of each posterior ingredient, alias/zero-edge behavior in real sessions, and whether another comparison model would help remain open.
finding_summary.results: All 435 preference fits converged, and every purchased batch changed relative to the passive raw-score GP on the same candidate pool. The model bought 3489 identities that its passive comparator would not have selected. On the 19559 non-tied pairs actually purchased, ordering accuracy was 63.79% versus 73.66%; every task/seed cell was worse. Full incumbent gain fell from 5.97807 to 4.45749, triggering both parts of the registered scientific falsifier despite successful execution and feedback. Late gain rose from 1.02241 to 1.69888, but did not recover the full-path loss. The complete endpoint mean fell from 0.60703 to 0.50566 (−0.10137): all three seed averages and all five task means were lower, with 13 of 15 individual endpoints lower. Population seed dispersion rose from 0.03018 to 0.05818. There were no missing tasks, numerical failures, invalid purchases or missing passive predictions.

molecular.headline: Rich heterocyclic chemistry, more large assemblies, and unresolved stereochemistry; several leaders carry unusual reactive groups
molecular.overall_character: Search-only assessment of n-aaeb1a1ac082 against published code Parent n-cf8d309c06de. The frozen context.comparison marks both child_complete and paired_complete true, with matched seeds 0/1/2 and no profile mismatch. All fifteen Child and fifteen Parent trajectory files were read: each session has 300 observations, including ten supplied initial molecules and 290 optimizer proposals. There are no missing paths or uncovered objectives. The observations below describe the actual submitted molecules and their supplied scores; they establish neither mechanism activation nor component attribution, biological efficacy, synthesis or an absent required pharmacophore. The Child spans substituted indoles/pyrazoles, nitrogen-rich fused aromatic systems, diaryl amines, enlarged carbonyl-rich nitrogen rings and polyacetal cages. Across 4,350 paid molecules its median heavy-atom count is 29, with 4,223 ring-containing and 3,901 aromatic-ring-containing graphs. This supports rich ring/aromatic labels while recognizing the saturated oxygen-rich branch. The digest ring-closure rates in fixed task order are 0.9839, 0.9793, 0.9529, 0.9816 and 0.9563; aromatic-text rates are 0.9793, 0.9782, 0.9276, 0.9782 and 0.6218. These are text counters, distinct from RDKit perception. The Child has 1,994 distinct nonempty typed and 1,289 generic Murcko scaffolds, with 127 empty scaffolds, versus Parent 1,667/951 and 95 empty. Thus this panel is structurally broad overall, although individual seeds concentrate on recognizable series. Child/Parent counts below six heavy atoms are 102/91, below twelve are 169/124, and above fifty are 176/44; the Child reaches 117 heavy atoms. In the late 2,175 paid molecules, defined as optimizer ordinals 146..290, those counts are 17/33, 22/45 and 61/3. Late nonempty typed/generic scaffold counts are 1,005/642 versus 774/414, with 20/36 empty scaffolds. The size tails coexist: the Child has fewer late fragments but substantially more large assemblies. Full-panel within-batch radius-2/2048/chiral bit-Morgan Tanimoto means are Child 0.300987 and Parent 0.411038 over 19,575 unordered pairs each; excluding pairs with either molecule below twelve heavy atoms gives 0.319774 over 18,118 pairs and 0.431990 over 18,484. Full within-session means are 0.249982/0.296088 over 628,575 pairs each, or 0.265316/0.311054 over 580,747/593,265 fragment-excluded pairs. These structural diagnostics do not themselves establish useful diversity or score benefit; full and late counts and denominators are retained in the audits. Common medicinal motifs support moderate drug-likeness, but synthetic plausibility is questionable: Child N-halogen/O-halogen/acyl-halide motif counts are 337/176/56 versus Parent 888/162/8. The reduced N-halogen count is a real chemical difference, not an across-the-board removal of reactive motifs. N-O single bonds occur in 647 Child graphs, a connectivity count that does not itself classify every N-O compound as unstable. All submitted optimizer graphs are formally neutral and lack assigned tetrahedral stereochemistry; RDKit identifies unassigned centers in 2,116 Child molecules. Neutral SMILES do not establish the protonation state used by the oracle or in solution. Evidence authority is the immutable request policy/requests/r0061-01-improve-L01-molecular-assess-fccce2fcb071a4c3.json, especially context.molecular_digest and context.citation_trajectory_paths. Derived evidence is policy/scratch/r0061-01-improve-L01/molecular/panel-chemistry.json and policy/scratch/r0061-01-improve-L01/molecular/pooled-similarity.json. The panel manifest enumerates all thirty exact input files, their Search seeds and SHA256 hashes. Its Child source files under policy/scratch/r0061-01-improve-L01/molecular/search_inputs/child/ are byte-identical derived copies of the trusted worktree staging trajectories, not published Child evidence. Parent inputs are the authoritative files under nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/seed-0, seed-1 and seed-2, each exact trajectory file named in that manifest. Per-cell audit filenames, quoted-molecule provenance, file existence, Search-seed checks and frozen-context validation are recorded in policy/scratch/r0061-01-improve-L01/molecular/validation.json. No Confirmation evidence, external pharmacophore or target structure was used.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 paid molecules are predominantly medium-sized aromatic heterocycles: median 25 heavy atoms, median three perceived rings and three aromatic rings. Seed 0 retains dimethoxy/vinyl indole carboxamides with a pyridyl amide partner. Seed 1 also reaches an ethoxy-substituted pyrazole bearing a phenol and thiocarbonyl-linked aniline; its best molecule has 24 heavy atoms. Other high examples carry methylthio substituents, pyridyl amides, partially saturated nitrogen rings or a benzene-fused small carbon ring. Seed 2 concentrates on fused benzimidazole/chroman-like frameworks with benzylic chlorides and sometimes aniline linkers. Conventional amide, ether and aryl building blocks are present, but strained ring fusions and benzylic halo/heteroatom arrangements make some members less straightforward synthetic targets. The typed/generic scaffold count is 382/203 versus Parent 186/69; N-halogen-containing graphs number 15 versus Parent 404. The Parent mostly retains indole-carbonyl/pyridyl or anilide architectures, including N-fluoro and N-chloro derivatives. Evidence: policy/scratch/r0061-01-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-0-zaleplon_mpo.json, audit-seed-1-zaleplon_mpo.json and audit-seed-2-zaleplon_mpo.json in the same directory; exact underlying files and hashes are in their input_provenance.
liabilities: Some high-scoring alternatives contain a strained fused carbon ring or potentially labile benzylic chloride; the trajectory gives no synthetic route or stability measurement.
Tiny halogen-containing fragments and large oxygen-rich conjugates remain in the paid stream despite extremely low scores.
missing_features: Consistent retention of a compact carbonyl-linked aromatic architecture is absent from the seed-2 leaders, although it occurs in seed 0 and in the paired Parent series. The favorable seed-1 thiocarbonyl branch prevents treating an amide as universally required.
The 315 stereogenic submitted graphs have no assigned configuration. No observed score comparison establishes a preferred stereoisomer.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The supplied initial trimethoxy indole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145. The Child seed-0 pyridyl amide scores 0.40282869817021466; the seed-1 pyrazole/phenol/thiocarbonyl compound reaches 0.45555627303128626. Adding a further phenolic oxygen to the latter series gives 0.4136551925282466, so simply adding oxygen is not favored in this local comparison. The seed-2 chlorobenzyl fused heterocycle reaches 0.34357172175619544. Parent leaders in seed order score 0.42348216717712805, 0.4387992465191 and 0.45050436981567554. Low Child extremes include chlorine at 0.0 and a very large indole/polyacetal conjugate at 8.950699084065816e-26. The observed gradient supports moderate-sized aromatic/heteroatom arrangements over both fragments and large appended cages, with multiple favorable motifs; it does not identify a single required heterocycle or prove that thiocarbonyl substitution alone drives the score.

per_task.generated_character: This is the largest and most aromatic Child output: median 36 heavy atoms and five perceived rings, with median four aromatic rings. Seed 0 develops fused pyridyl/chromone-like aromatic lactones bearing heteroaryl ethers and quinazoline-like substituents. Seed 1 favors enlarged pairs of nitrogen-rich fused dicarbonyl heterocycles linked through an unsaturated bridge; its leader has 42 heavy atoms. Seed 2 instead uses aminopyridine-rich molecules with arylamino links, methoxy groups, vinyl chains and frequent acyl fluoride or O-halogen termini. Ordinary aryl ethers and heteroaryl couplings look synthetically recognizable, but elaborate fused unions and reactive terminal groups make the whole population questionable as finished compounds. The Child has 98 molecules above fifty heavy atoms, versus Parent 18; late counts remain 54 versus 2. Evidence: policy/scratch/r0061-01-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-0-deco_hop.json, audit-seed-1-deco_hop.json and audit-seed-2-deco_hop.json in that directory.
liabilities: There are 25 acyl-halide-containing and 58 O-halogen-containing molecules; the cited high acyl fluoride is a reactive functional-group choice, not a validated stable product.
Extensive aromatic growth yields bulky molecules up to 117 heavy atoms, and late trajectories still spend observations above fifty heavy atoms.
missing_features: The Child does not reproduce the paired Parent seed-0 compact fused carbonyl/thione topology in its leaders. More appended aromatic units do not substitute for that particular arrangement in these observed scores; no universal desired core can be inferred.
Reliable preservation of ordinary ether/acyl chemistry is missing: a high-scoring matched decoration pair tolerates replacement of methoxy by an O-Cl group without any observed score distinction.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best initial score is 0.548381482770623. Child leaders score 0.6195899772209568, 0.5927736823629708 and 0.6072819700270681 in seed order, versus Parent 0.8561477222467935, 0.6217289889933668 and 0.6442339647723496. The seed-0 Child leader is a 31-heavy-atom heteroaryl ether/lactone assembly, whereas the 42-heavy-atom doubled core in seed 1 is lower. The seed-2 leader is a 24-heavy-atom aminopyridine with an unsaturated acyl fluoride. Methane and other tiny fragments sit at 0.5, so the apparent floor provides little chemical discrimination. A methoxy versus hypochlorite replacement in a decorated aminopyridine pair leaves the supplied score exactly 0.6026187405372063. Thus heteroaromatic arrangement and decoration correlate with the modest upward gradient, but mere size growth and chemically ordinary bond choice are not consistently rewarded. Parent seed 0 reaches a compact, differently fused N-rich carbonyl/thione architecture with an O-F group; its higher score is not evidence of superior synthesis.

per_task.generated_character: The paid set has median 31 heavy atoms, three perceived rings and two aromatic rings. Seed 0 leaders are relatively compact diaryl molecules with primary/secondary aminoalkyl chains, phenol or ether groups and carbon-bound halogens. Seed 1 develops much more constrained fused/bridged arylamine scaffolds bearing another saturated nitrogen ring, a flexible aminoethylaryl appendage and frequently N-hydroxylation. Seed 2 retains two chlorinated aromatic rings around an unsaturated chain, with phenols, aniline-like nitrogen, a terminal primary amine and carbonyl substituents. The Child clearly can produce saturated ring amines and aminoalkyl motifs; their absence is not the issue. The specified nonamide aliphatic-amine SMARTS matches 597/870 Child graphs versus Parent 722/870, a structural proxy rather than a pKa measurement. Some diaryl aminoalkyl products look makeable in principle, while the densely bridged N-hydroxylated branch has a much less obvious route. Evidence: policy/scratch/r0061-01-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-0-drd2_docking.json, audit-seed-1-drd2_docking.json and audit-seed-2-drd2_docking.json in that directory.
liabilities: The N-hydroxylated polycyclic leaders require consideration of N-O chemistry and stereochemical complexity; their high scores do not validate stability or synthesis.

The stream also contains 58 molecules above fifty heavy atoms, 47 below twelve, acyl-halide groups and O-halogen derivatives. These are liabilities of the emitted set, not a claim that every high scorer has them.
missing_features: The seed-2 leaders lack the constrained cyclic aminoalkyl geometry seen in the higher seed-1 and Parent seed-2 examples; they retain flexible or unsaturated bridges. This is a local association, not proof of a missing universal binding motif.

No submitted molecule specifies a charge state or tetrahedral configuration, despite 660 Child graphs with unassigned stereocenters. The top seed-1 graph has four unassigned centers; neither a preferred stereoisomer nor an optimal protonation state was evaluated explicitly in the submitted records.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Child leaders score 0.9724294268567502, 0.9831668737826238 and 0.7910311660754634 in seed order, versus Parent 0.980206046238846, 0.9999921067161532 and 0.9735180254338864. The initial best is 0.01904115112334333. A low N-sulfonyl pyrrolidine ketone scores 0.00021169315013374197; higher molecules combine aromatic regions with exposed aliphatic amine centers instead of sulfonamide-blocked ring nitrogen. This supports an association with accessible aminoalkyl functionality and its spacing, not a generic reward for any nitrogen or halogen. One matched seed-1 N-hydroxylated/dehydroxylated pair scores 0.9799202091803173 and 0.9620066745746968, respectively, so the observed scoring can favor the less ordinary N-O variant. The lower seed-2 endpoint despite an aminoalkyl group shows that amine presence alone is insufficient. Parent seed-2 reaches a more constrained cyclic-amine architecture, but this descriptive comparison does not identify topology as the causal driver.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 paid molecules have median 33 heavy atoms, four perceived rings and three aromatic rings. High seed-0 and seed-1 products combine two substituted phenyl groups, ethoxy/alkyl decoration and an enlarged partially unsaturated nitrogen-containing ring fused to a carbonyl-rich N-methyl ring. These are ketone/lactam/urea-like ring assemblies, not simple small heteroaromatics. Seed 2 explores quinoline-like rings linked to still larger N-rich carbonyl and oxygen/nitrogen ring systems; its best molecule has 41 heavy atoms. Ordinary amide/ether fragments are present, but nonstandard medium rings and bridged or spiro arrangements complicate synthesis. Typed/generic scaffold counts are 447/297 versus Parent 559/379, so this task does not share the panel-wide increase in scaffold counts. Evidence: policy/scratch/r0061-01-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-0-median_2.json, audit-seed-1-median_2.json and audit-seed-2-median_2.json in that directory.
liabilities: Medium-ring, bridged and spiro nitrogen/oxygen assemblies have no demonstrated synthetic route; 169 submitted graphs contain an N-O single bond, which requires inspecting the particular functional group rather than treating every such bond alike.
Tiny inorganic/organic fragments and peroxide-containing species occur at the low end, while ten proposals exceed fifty heavy atoms.
missing_features: The enlarged seed-2 structures do not reproduce the more compact fused amine/carbonyl arrangement of the paired Parent leader. Coherent joining of the aromatic and carbonyl-rich regions appears more relevant than adding still more ring atoms, but the trajectory does not establish a unique required motif.

Configuration is unspecified in 457 stereogenic Child graphs. More three-dimensional topology is already present; stereochemical definition, rather than a blanket shortage of saturated rings, is the missing representation.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial best score is 0.1678386594791329. Child leaders reach 0.2282301149059275, 0.2128343398267808 and 0.20279758019769495, against Parent 0.2228098910506594, 0.22127859918153825 and 0.24240057874100313. Methane and hydroxylamine each score 0.0, while methyl hydroperoxide scores 0.012140178546918842. The improvement accompanies combinations of aromatic regions with N-methyl carbonyl-rich rings, rather than isolated heteroatoms or small fragments. The Child seed-0 35-heavy-atom leader and its 34-heavy-atom analogue score 0.2282301149059275 and 0.22653939982357355, respectively: local ring-carbonyl arrangement matters even within a series. The larger 41-heavy-atom seed-2 leader is lower than the Parent 31-heavy-atom fused N-rich leader. This supports the importance of arrangement over indiscriminate growth, while the narrow observed score range cannot reveal a missing ideal structure.

per_task.generated_character: The Child median is 27 heavy atoms, four perceived rings and only one aromatic ring, reflecting sharply different seed chemistries. Seed 0 favors a fused N-rich dicarbonyl aromatic core with phenyl/benzyloxy substituents and a multiply fluorinated N-N appendage. Seed 1 couples a related N-fluorinated dicarbonyl core to an acetal-containing bridged ring and aryl or heteroaryl fragment. Seed 2 instead remains in densely bridged saturated polyacetal/thioacetal cages with C-F/C-Cl substitution and N-O connectivity; its leader has 27 heavy atoms, five perceived rings, no aromatic ring and eight unassigned stereocenters. These are not a uniform class of conventional fluorinated drug-like amines. Some C-bound multiple-halogen motifs are demonstrably generated: 46 molecules match that motif, so an inability to place multiple halogens on carbon would be an incorrect claim. The exotic N-fluorinated chain and complex mixed-acetal cages make synthetic plausibility particularly weak for the leaders. Evidence: policy/scratch/r0061-01-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-0-sitagliptin_mpo.json, audit-seed-1-sitagliptin_mpo.json and audit-seed-2-sitagliptin_mpo.json in that directory.
liabilities: The top molecule contains a highly unusual multiply fluorinated nitrogen chain and N-O connectivity; treating its score as evidence of a makeable, stable compound would be unwarranted.

The set contains 164 N-halogen motifs and 299 N-O single-bond motifs, while the seed-2 cages combine many unassigned stereocenters and mixed O/S/N ring connectivity. These are structural observations, not measured toxicity or stability.
missing_features: The seed-2 leaders lack the N-rich aromatic/imino-carbonyl organization present in the higher-scoring parallel and Parent branches, retaining oxygen-rich saturated cages instead. This is an observed architectural gap in that stream, not an unseen target-based pharmacophore prescription.

The output lacks stereochemical specification for the densely bridged cages and other stereogenic products; 590 of the 870 Child molecules have unassigned centers. No submitted-record comparison shows which configurations are desirable.

Stable, ordinary carbon-bound fluorinated alternatives are not absent, but their presence does not prevent high-scoring N-fluorinated N-N or N-F dicarbonyl derivatives. Chemical plausibility is not reliably preserved among the leaders.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial best is 0.0020944534688323298. Child leaders score 0.5086071370380201, 0.49198002116340644 and 0.17219695276927824, versus Parent 0.7658605860985803, 0.6443701453126088 and 0.6201223048692813. The Child extremes include a bulky amide-linked aromatic conjugate at 3.2416258040348776e-69 and an oversized oxygen-rich cage at 4.0992319975355965e-41. Smaller N-rich fluorinated structures are higher than those large assemblies, and the aromatic dicarbonyl branches are higher than the saturated cage branch in the observed seeds. The Parent leaders are smaller imino/carbonyl N-rich fused systems with fluorinated carbon substituents or cyclic amines; they too can bear N-F groups. The current scores therefore support a favorable size/heteroatom/aromatic balance in some branches, but do not establish that N-fluorination, any single heterocycle or a named amine is itself required. The most conspicuous high-scoring Child molecule remains chemically unusual.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-aaeb1a1ac082, compared with n-cf8d309c06de, under the same Search seeds 0/1/2 and 300 observations per session including ten initial records. Across 4,350 paid graphs, the Child contains 337 N-halogen, 176 O-halogen and 56 acyl-halide motifs versus Parent 888, 162 and 8. A cited methoxy/hypochlorite pair has exactly equal supplied scores, and a cited high-scoring N-rich leader bears a multiply fluorinated N-N chain. Late counts remain 287, 109 and 38 over 2,175 graphs. These source-specific findings are from policy/scratch/r0061-01-improve-L01/molecular/panel-chemistry.json and its exact-input manifest. Carbon multiple-halogen motifs are present in 49 Child graphs and 24 Parent graphs; there is no evidence for an absolute inability to generate them. This is a chemistry association, not attribution to the changed model component.
transferable_gaps.gap: The emitted set does not consistently preserve chemically ordinary functional-group connectivity when decorating otherwise recognizable scaffolds.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A transferable chemistry capability would distinguish carbon halogenation, heteroatom halogenation and acyl activation by their local bonding context, while retaining coherent stable alternatives around useful scaffolds. It should be able to express functional-group-aware edits without assuming every N-O bond is invalid or treating the present motif counts as an objective. Whether that capability helps must remain determined by legal current-session feedback; these observations justify neither a hidden-identity branch nor a universal motif ban.

transferable_gaps.evidence: For n-aaeb1a1ac082 on Search seeds 0/1/2, the digest reports zero stereocentre-text and charge-text rates throughout the 4,350 paid graphs. Independent RDKit perception in policy/scratch/r0061-01-improve-L01/molecular/panel-chemistry.json finds 2,116 Child molecules with unassigned tetrahedral centers and zero with assigned centers; all have zero formal charge. The corresponding Parent counts are 2,425 unassigned and zero assigned, also with neutral submitted graphs. A cited bridged cage leader has eight unassigned centers and a cited polycyclic aminoalkyl leader has four. These observations concern submitted structures, not an assertion that neutral molecules stay uncharged in solution or that the oracle omitted its own preparation.
transferable_gaps.gap: Generated stereogenic structures are never submitted with defined tetrahedral configuration, and explicit ionic representations are absent.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic representation would need to preserve and propose explicit configurations when stereogenic connectivity is created, and support chemically meaningful charge states when appropriate. Any benefit requires score evidence on such alternatives within the allowed session. Neither a preferred stereoisomer nor a preferred protonation state follows from these unspecified inputs.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-aaeb1a1ac082 versus published n-cf8d309c06de, matched Search seeds 0/1/2 and 290 paid observations per session. The Child has 169 graphs below twelve heavy atoms and 176 above fifty, versus Parent 124 and 44; Child size reaches 117 heavy atoms. Late counts are 22/61 versus Parent 45/3, so a reduction of late fragments coexists with excess large assemblies. Its 1,994 typed and 1,289 generic nonempty scaffolds exceed Parent 1,667 and 951, yet the quoted low-score examples include oversized conjugates and cages, while several cited leaders are compact multifunctional aromatic or aminoalkyl compounds. The full and late denominators and exact sources are retained in policy/scratch/r0061-01-improve-L01/molecular/panel-chemistry.json. Size and scaffold counts are descriptive associations only, not a component attribution or evidence that maximizing scaffold diversity improves an endpoint.
transferable_gaps.gap: Structural exploration does not reliably keep growth and fragmentation within coherent, moderate-sized molecular architectures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The missing output capability is controlled remodeling of a coherent functional arrangement: substantial ring or linker alternatives that preserve useful neighboring chemistry without indiscriminate duplication or collapse. Any proposal mechanism addressing this should keep size tails and fragment-excluded diversity as diagnostics, with usefulness learned from current-session scores. The observations do not justify a hard size cutoff, a size reward, or suppressing an entire valid molecular class.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
